# `table3_records`

**Table III records**

One row per classification record on one act's OLRC Table III page: which U.S. Code place each section of a public law went to, as the page states it. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

**Coverage.** Sampled. Measured on one cold-start run (receipt `d1-measured-run-2026-09-19/`), and the measurement is mostly a refusal: of the 106 public acts the law route listed (108 laws, less the 2 private laws, which are not requested), 2 were read and produced 65 rows, 5 were refused, and the walk then stopped for the Congress with 99 acts unread — the per-run cap of 300 was never approached. Since 2026-09-24 the rollup reads one Table III page per act on each scoped Congress's chain, under that cap, from the highest act already published. It asks for that act again only to read the act its page names. *(measured 2026-09-19)*

**Data quality.** Table III holds an act only once OLRC has classified it, and holds no page for an act that classified nothing. It lags enactment by tens of laws: on 2026-09-24 it was current through 119-73 while the law route reached 119-111, and 33 of the acts at or before 119-73 had no page (receipt `drift-audit-2026-09-24/laws/`). OLRC answers such an act with `200 OK` and a connection dropped inside its site menu. Those bytes are a prefix of a served page, so the answer cannot tell an act the table does not hold from a served page cut short.
So the rollup follows Table III's own chain instead of asking for every law, with spicy-docs' iter_table3_chain (B32), which owns the rules below. Each served page names the next act the table holds (119-4 names 119-12). Each run asks again for the Congress's highest published act, only to read the act it names; its rows are not published again. Cold, the run starts at the lowest act the law route lists. It then asks for each act the pages name. The chain ends at a page that names no next act, or names one the laws table does not list, or one past the release point the page states. A chain act that does not serve (a transport failure after the acquirer's retries, or a page the reader refuses) ends its Congress's chain for the run. Three in a row end the walk, and it starts no request after 20 minutes. A Congress whose lowest listed act has no page cannot start cold. A run asks one page per Congress when the table has not moved, plus one for each act a new release adds.
Until 2026-09-24 the rollup asked for every law and counted each act without a page as a refusal, so from 2026-09-22 every run stopped at 119-5 and the table held only the 65 rows of acts 119-1 and 119-4. A capped live walk along the chain from 119-4 read 119-12, 119-18, 119-21, 119-22 and 119-23 (643 rows) in six requests, asking no act without a page (receipt `table3-walk-2026-09-24/chain/`).
An act's rows are published once: a later edit to its page (a status moving to repealed) is not picked up, and `release_point` says how current the captured page was. Private laws and pre-1957 session-law chapters are not requested. `usc_section_key` is `usc_section` folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and Table III itself prints some sections both ways (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`). Because an act's rows are published once, rows published before the column existed keep it NULL; fold their `usc_section` by the same rule to join them. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

- **Parquet file:** `table3_records.parquet`
- **MCP `query_sql` support:** Configured; requires an available artifact.
- **Publication status:** Not established by this schema page or its measurement date.

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `act_key` | `VARCHAR` | The act key requested: a public law number, or a pre-1957 session-law chapter. |
| `stated_key` | `VARCHAR` | The act key as the page itself states it, en dash and all. |
| `seq` | `VARCHAR` | Zero-based position of this record on the page. |
| `congress` | `VARCHAR` | The Congress the page states for the act. |
| `act_date` | `VARCHAR` | The act's date as the page states it. |
| `statutes_at_large_volume` | `VARCHAR` | The volume the page states for the act. |
| `release_point` | `VARCHAR` | The currency the page states in its Table III Tool banner. |
| `act_section` | `VARCHAR` | The act section this record classifies. |
| `record_volume` | `VARCHAR` | The volume in this record's own statviewer link, where it carries one. |
| `record_page` | `VARCHAR` | The Statutes at Large page for this record. |
| `usc_title` | `VARCHAR` | The Code title the section went to; NULL where it went nowhere. |
| `usc_section` | `VARCHAR` | The Code section the section went to; NULL where it went nowhere. |
| `status` | `VARCHAR` | The page's status column for the record (repealed, omitted, and the like). |
| `observed_at` | `VARCHAR` | When the page was captured; the merge prefers the larger value. |
| `usc_section_key` | `VARCHAR` | usc_section as a join key: lower-cased, with every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen, as RefSpec's section oracle keys it. Fold the other side the same way (schemas.tables.usc_section_key): document_citations' usc_section rule 001 keeps the printed case and dashes. NULL where usc_section is, and on rows published before the column existed. |
